title: Winter Prep Coach
subtitle: 12V battery, coolant/antifreeze, and snow-ready tires — one calm checklist before the cold snap.
tone: Production EN coach (US/EU): warm mentor, visual-first, max 2 CTAs, progress %, mileage personalization, legal disclaimer every step, high-risk modal with Find a nearby shop cancel. Phase 2 winter: cold-weather battery, coolant, snow tires; never open hot cooling systems.

prerequisites: Plan for snow tires or quality winters if you see ice regularly
tools_checklist: Jack + stands + torque wrench (if swapping wheels)
parts_checklist: Correct coolant if topping/flushing via shop
Winter / snow tire set or all-weathers rated for snow
Ice scraper, washer fluid rated for freeze point

adaptive_rules.coach_note: Snow-belt driving: dedicated winter tires beat worn all-seasons once temps stay near freezing.
EV winter: precondition while plugged in, expect range loss, and keep the 12V healthy — cold kills weak 12Vs.
Tesla winter: Scheduled Departure + precondition; watch 12V warnings; use winters if you see regular ice.
Diesel: confirm fuel/anti-gel strategy per manual and glow-plug health — cold starts are unforgiving.
Higher-mile winter prep: prioritize battery test and coolant condition — roadside fails spike in cold snaps.

risk_confirm.title: Battery testing in cold weather
risk_confirm.body: Batteries can emit explosive gas. Wear eye protection. On hybrids/EVs only use designated 12V points — never orange HV. If access is unclear, find a nearby shop.

steps.title: Weak battery — winter priority
steps.coach_encourage: Replacing before a cold snap beats a parking-lot jump. Good catch. Nice momentum — you're about 25% through.
steps.personalize: Your {{model}} at {{mileage}} miles may need a 12V before {{next_service}} miles.
steps.description: Charge/test confirm, then replace with the correct type (AGM if required). Euro cars may need registration. EVs: prefer qualified install.
steps.safety_disclaimer: General guidance only. Follow your owner's manual or an authorized tech. This app isn't liable for DIY damage.

steps.title: Coolant / antifreeze — cold engine only
steps.coach_encourage: This step is important — only check when the engine is cold. You're crushing it — roughly 38% done.
steps.personalize: Coolant check for your {{make}} at {{mileage}} miles. Recheck freeze protection before {{next_service}} miles.
steps.description: On a cold engine, reservoir should sit between MIN and MAX. Confirm the coolant type in the manual — mixing chemistries can damage the system. Freeze-point testing is ideal before deep cold.
steps.safety_warning: Never remove a hot radiator cap. Pressurized coolant causes severe burns.
steps.trust_nudge: If you're unsure about anything, stop and find a nearby shop — that's the smart call, not quitting.

risk_confirm.title: Cooling system burn hazard
risk_confirm.body: Opening a hot or pressurized cooling system can cause severe burns. Only inspect when fully cool. Coolant disposal and full flushes should follow local rules — when unsure, find a nearby shop.

variants.description: Some BEVs use dedicated thermal loops — still only service when cool and per manual. Pack coolant work is shop-only.
variants.safety_warning: Do not open EV thermal loops unless the manual shows an owner reservoir.

steps.title: Coolant needs attention

steps.description: Top off only with the exact spec if the manual allows owner top-ups. Pink/green/blue are not interchangeable. Repeated loss = leak diagnosis at a shop.

risk_confirm.title: Wheel swap & jacking risk
risk_confirm.body: Incorrect jacking or lug torque can cause injury or wheel loss. Use rated jack stands on manufacturer points and torque to the door-sticker specification. If anything feels unstable, stop and find a nearby shop.
